/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 23 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2660 (-33)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3791 (-57)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2109 (-42)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1887 (-3)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1020 (0)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market ended the week on a notably quieter and softer note following several days of improving sentiment across both basins. The BCI 182 5TC fell by $519 to $34,380, while the C5 index eased by $0.090 to $14.10 and C3 slipped by $0.180 to $33.865. In the Pacific, activity was limited, with conditions remaining broadly steady despite a quieter session. Just one miner was active on C5, reportedly bidding $13.50 against offers in the low $14s, having fixed a handful of vessels around $14.15 the previous day. With little fresh demand emerging, the market lacked the momentum seen earlier in the week. The Atlantic was similarly subdued, with limited activity leaving the market lacking direction. Although $34.50 was reported paid yesterday for a 20–26 November C3, rumours of a $33.25 fixing for 15–20 November added to the softer sentiment. Overall, the market closed the week on a quieter footing, with the recent upward momentum giving way to a more cautious tone as activity tapered off.
PANAMAX
The market ended the week on a subdued note, with further losses recorded across both basins and the Atlantic continuing to bear the brunt of the downward pressure. Trans-Atlantic activity remained limited, with sources reporting a lack of fresh cargo enquiry and an increasingly competitive tonnage list allowing charterers to maintain control of negotiations. Despite some owners said to be showing greater resistance to further reductions, the imbalance between available vessels and cargo requirements continued to weigh on rates, with prompt tonnage particularly exposed. Market sources highlighted that conditions in EC South America remained challenging, with an abundance of available tonnage competing for relatively few cargoes, leaving little indication of an immediate change in sentiment. In the Pacific, the market continued to demonstrate greater resilience, although momentum appeared to be easing as the week drew to a close. North Pacific grain requirements and Australian coal movements provided some underlying support, with recent fixing activity suggesting charterers were still prepared to pay comparatively healthy levels for suitable tonnage. The P5TC declined by a further $377 today to close the week at $18,981.
SUPRAMAX
A gentle slide into the weekend with limited activity, the 11TC average was down $42 to finish the week at $23,849, which was $276 up overall from last Friday. Asia remains firm, with backhaul routes dominating the North Pacific and Indonesia posting steady gains, resulting in continued strong period rates. Topsheen were said to have taken an Ultramax in North China for short period in the mid $20,000’s, however further details didn’t come to light, and the Fuji Maru (63,682 2026) Yokkaichi 1-5 November was reported fixed for 12 months at $21,500, but sources said this must have failed as the Owners were now using the vessel for own business. Elsewhere the Viet Thuan 56-02 (55,709 2006) Dongfang fixed a trip to Bangladesh intention clinker at a strong $32,000 and the St Ajisai (61,105 2022) Chittagong 28 October was placed on subjects basis delivery Singapore for a trip via Indonesia to Thailand at $24,750 by Norden.
HANDYSIZE
Following several active days, the market saw a relatively quiet session. The BHSI held unchanged at 1,020, while the 7TC average edged up by $4 to close at $18,361. Rates across the Continent and Mediterranean was generally soft, edging slightly below the previous levels. The South Atlantic maintained steady momentum, supported by fresh demand. By contrast, the US Gulf showed signs of slowing activity and awaited a pickup in demand to sustain current levels. The Manta Kerem (37,046 2015) open Altamira, as fixed by Oldendorff for an inter-Caribbean trip at around $15,000–$16,000, although further details were not disclosed. The Pacific was again quiet but balanced, with a steady cargo book and a shorter tonnage list. The Paiwan Hero (39,654 2026) was placed on subjects for delivery Caldera and a trip via the North Pacific to the Continent with clean cargo at $23,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
US Weekly Grain Exports

In the week to 15 October, US combined exports of corn, wheat, soy (beans and meal) and sorghum rose 0.2 Mt from the preceding week to 3.4 Mt, although marked a 0.7 Mt year-on-year decrease, USDA data show. The decline was led by corn shipments, which fell 0.6 Mt year-on-year to 0.8 Mt. Wheat exports also dropped 0.4 Mt to 0.2 Mt, while soy (beans+meal) exports rose 0.3 Mt to 2.3 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape recovered from early weakness, with Nov and Dec strengthening through the afternoon and good volume across the front months. Nov opened at 35,250 before dipping to 34,800, then rallied to 35,700, with heavy afternoon volume around 35,250–35,500, last trading at 35,550. Dec opened at 35,000 before strengthening to 35,600, with significant activity around 35,250–35,500. Q4 26 improved from 34,500 to 34,650, while Q1 27 traded between 28,000–28,250, last printing at 28,200. Q2 27 eased from 33,650 to 33,500. Cal 27 traded between 31,250–31,400.

PMX
PMX saw a mixed session, with Nov recovering from early weakness while Dec and the forward quarters remained under pressure. Nov opened at 18,500 before dipping to 18,450, then strengthened to 18,850 late, with heavy volume around 18,600 and good closing activity at the highs. Dec opened at 18,700 before falling to 18,200, with significant volume around 18,200–18,350, finishing at the higher end. Q4 26 improved from 19,000 to 19,150, while Q1 27 weakened from 16,350 to 16,200 before recovering to 16,350. Q2 27 traded between 17,650–17,800. Cal 27 eased from 16,775 to 16,750.

SMX + HANDY
SMX held a firmer tone across the front months, with heavy activity in Nov and Dec as prices strengthened through the morning. Nov opened at 20,100 before rallying to 20,400, with significant volume around 20,150–20,400, before easing to 20,250 late. Dec traded between 19,500–19,650, last printing at 19,650. Q4 26 improved from 20,250 to 20,300, while Q1 27 traded between 15,800–16,000, with good late volume at 16,000. Cal 27 printed at 15,750.
